hints: Focus on what type of reaction happens between a C4 acid and an alcohol with concentrated H2SO4.
Remember the ester product must keep the propyl group from propan-1-ol as the O-CH2CH2CH3 part, so count carbons on the left of the O in S, T and U.
Now count carbons on the right of the C=O to see which comes from a straight chain C4 carboxylic acid, and think about why the branched C4 acid gives no match.
walkthrough:
**Spot the esterification**

Great start. Carboxylic acid + alcohol with concentrated H2SO4 gives an ester + water. So Z must be a carboxylic acid of formula $C_4H_8O_2$.

$$\text{carboxylic acid} + \text{propan-1-ol} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. } H_2SO_4} \text{propyl ester} + H_2O$$

**Work out the possible acids for Z**

There are two carboxylic acids with formula $C_4H_8O_2$. That is butanoic acid, $CH_3CH_2CH_2COOH$, and branched 2-methylpropanoic acid, $(CH_3)_2CHCOOH$.

With propan-1-ol, $CH_3CH_2CH_2OH$, they would give $CH_3CH_2CH_2COOCH_2CH_2CH_3$ (propyl butanoate, straight chain) and $(CH_3)_2CHCOOCH_2CH_2CH_3$ (propyl 2-methylpropanoate, branched).

**Count carbons in S, T and U**

In a skeletal ester, count each bend as carbon. The left side of the O must be propyl (3 carbons) because it comes from propan-1-ol.

S is propyl propanoate ($C_3$ acid part), T is propyl butanoate ($C_4$ acid part), U is butyl butanoate ($C_4$ alcohol part). Only T matches a straight chain C4 acid plus propan-1-ol, and the branched C4 product is not shown at all.

options.A: S is propyl propanoate. Its acid part has only 3 carbons in total (propanoic acid), so it would need Z to be C3H6O2, not C4H8O2. T is correct but S is not, so this pair is wrong.
options.B: U has a butyl group on the alcohol side (O-CH2CH2CH2CH3). That would need butan-1-ol as reactant, but we only have propan-1-ol. U cannot be formed here.
options.C: S comes from the wrong acid and U comes from the wrong alcohol. S needs a C3 acid and U needs a C4 alcohol, so neither fits Z (C4 acid) + propan-1-ol.
options.D: T is propyl butanoate, CH3CH2CH2COOCH2CH2CH3. The left propyl comes from propan-1-ol and the right butanoyl comes from straight chain butanoic acid, one isomer of Z. The other isomer of Z would give a branched ester which is not drawn, so T only is possible.
